name: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE)
intro: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) 是面向人类知识前沿的多模态封闭式学术基准。其公开集包含 2,500 道由全球近 1,000 名专家贡献的问题，覆盖 100 多个学科，并另设私有留出集检查过拟合与投机。题目经过前沿模型难度筛选、研究生级同行评审和组织者终审，最终以准确率与置信度校准误差评估模型。
org: Center for AI Safety and collaborating institutions
build_method: 全球专家征题、前沿模型门槛、两轮专家评审
task_type: 多项选择题、精确匹配简答题
eval_feature: 前沿模型筛选、私有留出审计、置信度校准
scale: 2,500 个公开问题，另有私有留出集
task_type_en: Multiple choice and exact-match short answer
build_method_en: Global expert submissions, frontier-model gating, and two rounds of expert review
eval_feature_en: Frontier-model filtering, private held-out auditing, and confidence calibration
intro_en: Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) is a multimodal closed-ended academic benchmark targeting the frontier of human knowledge. Its public set contains 2,500 questions contributed by nearly 1,000 experts across more than 100 subjects, with a separate private held-out set for detecting overfitting and gaming. Questions pass frontier-model difficulty gates, graduate-level peer review, and organizer approval, and models are evaluated with accuracy and confidence calibration error.
scale_en: 2,500 public questions plus a private held-out set

drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2501.14249, Sections 3-4 and Appendices B.1 and C.1. HLE draws questions from nearly 1,000 expert contributors at more than 500 institutions in 50 countries. Submissions include the question, answer specification, detailed rationale, subject, contributor, and affiliation, and must be precise, original, closed-ended, non-searchable, and easily verifiable. Exact-match items must stump every frontier model; multiple-choice items must stump all but at most one. More than 70,000 model attempts send about 13,000 questions to human review. Round one gives each question one to three graduate-level reviews and iterative author feedback; round two requires organizer or trained-expert approval. The public 2,500-question set spans more than 100 subjects, with about 14% multimodal and 24% multiple choice, while a private held-out set checks overfitting and gaming. Evaluation requests reasoning, a final answer, and 0-100% confidence; an O3-mini structured judge accepts equivalent answer formats, and reports accuracy plus RMS calibration error.
